title.zh: 体积归一化高斯源剖面

summary: Discrete volume-normalized Gaussian source profile on a nonuniform normalized-radius cell grid

capability: Discrete volume-normalized Gaussian source profile on a nonuniform normalized-radius cell grid.
operation: Build a volume-normalized Gaussian radial profile
(rho_norm, vpr, drho_norm, center, width, total) -> profile
discovery.model: Discrete normalized radial source shape with denominator floor max(2 width^2, float64 tiny) and exact supplied-volume normalization; extended intermediate arithmetic.
discovery.geometry: Normalized radial cell grid with explicit volume metric and quadrature weights; rho_norm is a dimensionless normalized radius.
discovery.boundary: Discrete cell-volume sum with no extrapolation or hidden endpoint reconstruction; the supplied total sets the volume normalization.

identity.relation: Discrete Gaussian source with denominator floor max(2 width^2, float64 tiny) and exact supplied-volume normalization
identity.definition: Let D=max(2*width^2, float64 tiny). Set S_i=exp(-((rho_i-center)^2-min_j((rho_j-center)^2))/D), using a factored difference of squares. Return total*S_i/sum_j(S_j*vpr_j*drho_norm_j). At subnormal widths the floor retains the repaired source numerical convention rather than exact unfloored continuous Gaussian samples.
identity.model: Discrete normalized radial source shape with float64 output and extended intermediate arithmetic
identity.geometry: Normalized radial cell grid with explicit volume metric and quadrature weights
identity.boundary: Discrete cell-volume sum; no extrapolation or hidden endpoint reconstruction
assumptions: All grid vectors are equal-length, finite and one-dimensional.
Width is scalar; signed finite widths are accepted because the Gaussian is even.

inputs.name: rho_norm
inputs.dtype: Python/NumPy real integer or floating array converted to float64; boolean, complex, string and masked inputs rejected

inputs.name: drho_norm
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; same shape as rho_norm.

inputs.name: center
inputs.constraints: Finite real scalar; may lie outside [0,1].

inputs.name: width
inputs.constraints: Finite nonzero real scalar for finite result; zero/nonfinite return NaNs.

outputs.name: profile
outputs.constraints: Finite on successful return for finite nonzero widths; zero/nonfinite width returns all NaN.

preconditions: All grid vectors are equal-length, finite and one-dimensional.
Width is scalar; signed finite widths are accepted because the Gaussian is even.
supported: Nonuniform grids, conservation, signed/integer/tiny widths, remote centers and malformed inputs.
excluded: No continuous quadrature claim beyond supplied cell weights.
No source-parameter validation beyond the declared scalar/grid contract.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for malformed types/shapes, nonfinite grid, center or total, or nonpositive weights. After those checks, a width of zero, NaN or either infinity returns an all-NaN profile.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises FloatingPointError for overflowed finite output or when rounding the float64 profile loses the requested discrete integral beyond 64 float64 epsilons relative, with zero absolute tolerance. Negligible tails may underflow to zero.

python.signature: gaussian_profile(rho_norm, vpr, drho_norm, *, center, width, total)

example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.source import gaussian_profile
r=np.array([.2,.6]); v=np.array([2.,3.]); d=np.array([.4,.6])
p=gaussian_profile(r,v,d,center=.5,width=.2,total=4.)
assert np.isclose(np.sum(p*v*d),4.)

scope: Nonuniform grids, conservation, signed/integer/tiny widths, remote centers and malformed inputs.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent numerical probes establish the named mathematical relation, discrete conservation, boundary and shape/failure behavior. They do not establish general plasma calibration or complete edge-model validity.
known_limitations: No continuous quadrature claim beyond supplied cell weights.
No source-parameter validation beyond the declared scalar/grid contract.
Extended-intermediate checks were executed on Linux x86_64 with NumPy longdouble; platforms whose longdouble has no extended range are not computationally qualified for extreme-scale cases.
No array-parameter broadcasting or batch axis: all grid inputs are equal-length vectors and profile parameters are scalar-shaped.
